## Hybrid Retrieval

Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical search (e.g. BM25) with dense vector search, then merges the two ranked result sets, often via reciprocal rank fusion, to capture both exact term matches and semantic similarity. 

It consistently outperforms either method alone on queries mixing rare identifiers (error codes, product SKUs) with natural language intent, and has become the default retrieval pattern in production RAG systems.

## Ranking Methods

Hybrid retrieval typically uses reciprocal rank fusion to merge results from multiple search methods into a single ranked list.
